definitions.explanation: The fourth finger, between the middle finger and the little finger. Called 薬指 ('medicine finger') because it was traditionally used to apply powdered medicine.

examples.japanese: {薬指|くすりゆび}に{指輪|ゆびわ}をしている。
examples.english: She's wearing a ring on her ring finger.

examples.japanese: {左手|ひだりて}の{薬指|くすりゆび}に{結婚指輪|けっこんゆびわ}をはめた。
examples.english: I put a wedding ring on my left ring finger.

examples.japanese: ギターを{弾|ひ}くとき、{薬指|くすりゆび}が{思|おも}うように{動|うご}かなくて{苦労|くろう}した。
examples.english: When playing guitar, I struggled because my ring finger wouldn't move the way I wanted.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
The name {薬指|くすりゆび} literally means 'medicine finger.' In traditional Japanese and Chinese medicine, this finger was used to apply and mix powdered medicines because it was believed to have a gentle touch.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {薬指|くすりゆび}に{指輪|ゆびわ}をはめる (to put a ring on one's ring finger)
- {左手|ひだりて}の{薬指|くすりゆび} (left ring finger — where wedding rings are worn)
- {右手|みぎて}の{薬指|くすりゆび} (right ring finger)

RELATED WORDS:
The five fingers in order: {親指|おやゆび} (thumb), {人|ひと}{差|さ}し{指|ゆび} (index finger), {中指|なかゆび} (middle finger), {薬指|くすりゆび} (ring finger), {小指|こゆび} (little finger/pinky).
